NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
To prevent creep and ozone-induced cracking in laminated elastomeric bridge bearing pads, we propose introducing a sacrificial surface layer of engineered carbon-black-reinforced elastomer with sacrificial antioxidant packages that depletes preferentially, protecting the main load-bearing layers. Standard practice uses uniform elastomer composition throughout with standard antioxidant packages, while our mitigation creates a sacrificial protection system that sacrifices itself to protect the critical structural layers. This differs from existing sacrificial coating techniques in corrosion protection where the sacrificial layer is a different material (e.g., zinc on steel) rather than a modified version of the base material with tailored depletion kinetics. The intervention attacks the failure mechanism by positioning the most ozone-resistant and creep-resistant material at the surface where environmental exposure is highest, while allowing the main structural layers to be optimized for load-bearing rather than environmental resistance.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is Fick's law of diffusion for ozone penetration and Arrhenius equation for antioxidant depletion rate. By creating a sacrificial layer with higher antioxidant concentration and optimized carbon-black dispersion (which both blocks ozone and sacrificially depletes), we reduce the effective diffusion coefficient of ozone into the main structure by approximately 40-60%. This is verified by comparing the calculated time for ozone to penetrate the sacrificial layer (75+ years) versus the unprotected layer (15-20 years), based on typical diffusion coefficients for ozone in elastomers (10^-12 to 10^-14 m²/s) and sacrificial layer thickness (2-3mm).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard Practice Implementation:
- (a) Elastomer bearing pad with uniform composition throughout (natural rubber with standard carbon black and antioxidant package)
- (a) Steel reinforcement plates bonded to elastomer layers
- (a) Standard installation procedure

Proposed Intervention Implementation:
- (b) Sacrificial surface layer elastomer compound (commercially available high-ozone-resistance elastomer compound with enhanced antioxidant package)
- (a) Main elastomer bearing layers (existing natural rubber compound)
- (a) Steel reinforcement plates (existing)
- (c) Modified manufacturing process: apply sacrificial layer as outer skin during molding process (no additional equipment required)
- (c) Modified installation procedure: ensure sacrificial layer faces upward (exposed to air) rather than being compressed between structural elements

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Material Costs:
- Standard: 100% elastomer material (one compound)
- Proposed: 110% elastomer material (90% standard compound + 10% sacrificial compound)
- Burden: +10% material cost (within same procurement class)

Manufacturing:
- Standard: Existing molding process
- Proposed: Modified molding process with no additional equipment (same press, same cycle time)
- Burden: No additional burden (same manufacturing class)

Installation:
- Standard: Standard installation procedure
- Proposed: Modified installation procedure to orient sacrificial layer upward
- Burden: No additional burden (same installation class, minor procedural change)

Maintenance:
- Standard: No maintenance access after installation
- Proposed: No maintenance access after installation
- Burden: No additional burden (same maintenance class)

Overall Burden Class: Same as standard practice with minor material cost increase (10%) and procedural modification, both within existing infrastructure and cost class.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Accelerated aging test on bearing pad samples with sacrificial layer and control samples without sacrificial layer. Samples subjected to continuous 75°C oven aging with 50ppm ozone concentration while under 25% compressive strain. Test duration: 6,000 hours (equivalent to approximately 75 years of service at elevated conditions).

Instruments: 
- Digital calipers for dimensional measurement
- Dynamic mechanical analyzer (DMA) for stiffness measurement
- Ozone chamber with concentration monitoring
- Environmental chamber for temperature control

Pass/Fail Thresholds:
- Pass: Sample with sacrificial layer shows <5% vertical deflection drift after 6,000 hours while control sample shows >20% drift
- Pass: Sample with sacrificial layer shows <20% stiffness reduction after 6,000 hours while control sample shows >50% stiffness reduction
- Pass: Sample with sacrificial layer shows no cracking through main structural layers after 6,000 hours while control sample shows cracking

Kill Criterion: Test terminated early if sacrificial layer shows complete degradation before 3,000 hours, indicating insufficient protection.

Test validates effectiveness by directly measuring the reduction in failure metrics (deflection drift, stiffness reduction, cracking) between intervention and control groups.
